applies_why: The judge text gives UNDERDETERMINED for a single passage and reasons from its two phrases, so it is doing the thing K-S2 governs.
quote: D4 vs C2 (Luke 2:48-49): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4; Mary's phrase "thy father" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to "my Father's business."
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: "A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand." I weighed (1) a two-sense verse may make the issue UNDERDETERMINED/open versus (2) K-S2 forbids treating it as open and requires both senses to stand.
why: The judge marks the point UNDERDETERMINED by treating Luke 2:48-49's "thy father" as qualified by "my Father's business," which turns a two-sense verse into an open/underdetermined matter contrary to K-S2.
